questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice of the following sentence: 'The teacher is explaining the grammar rules to the students.'
options: The grammar rules are explained to the students by the teacher.
The students are being explained the grammar rules by the teacher.
The grammar rules are being explained to the students by the teacher.
The grammar rules were explained to the students by the teacher.
questions.explanation: In present continuous tense ('is explaining'), the passive structure is 'is/are/am + being + past participle'. Thus, 'are being explained' is correct.
questions.subject: English Language

questions.question: Match the idioms in Column I with their correct meanings in Column II:
questions.explanation: A blessing in disguise means a misfortune that turns out to be good (III); Burn the midnight oil means working late (I); Piece of cake means very easy (IV); Spill the beans means reveal a secret (II).
columnII: (I) Work or study hard late into the night
(III) Something good that isn't recognized at first
(IV) A task that can be accomplished very easily
questions.subject: English Language

questions.question: Directions: Given below are Assertion [As] and Reason [R]. Choose the correct option:
options: Both [As] and [R] are true, and [R] is the correct explanation of [As].
Both [As] and [R] are true, but [R] is not the correct explanation of [As].
questions.explanation: 'Neither' is singular, so it requires the singular verb 'was' instead of 'were'. Therefore, both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason correctly explains Assertion.
questions.assertion: The sentence 'Neither of the boys were present at the meeting' is grammatically incorrect in standard English.
questions.reason: Pronouns like 'neither', 'either', and 'each' are singular and must be followed by a singular verb.
questions.subject: English Language

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding Direct and Indirect Speech and select the correct option:
questions.explanation: Statement 2 is incorrect because universal truths and habitual facts do NOT change their tense even when the reporting verb is in the past tense. Statements 1, 3, and 4 are standard rules of narration.
statements: When the reporting verb is in the past tense, all present tenses in the direct speech are changed to the corresponding past tenses in indirect speech.
Universal truths and habitual facts undergo a change of tense even if the reporting verb is in the past tense.
Words expressing nearness in time or place are generally changed into words expressing distance in indirect speech (e.g., 'now' becomes 'then').
Interrogative sentences in direct speech are changed into assertive sentences in indirect speech, removing question marks.
questions.subject: English Language

questions.question: Identify the one-word substitution for: 'A person who knows everything or all things.'
questions.explanation: 'Omniscient' means knowing everything (all-knowing). Omnipotent means all-powerful; omnipresent means present everywhere; optimist looks at the bright side.
questions.subject: English Language

questions.question:
Rearrange the following sentence segments (P, Q, R, S) to form a meaningful sentence:
P: in the modern world
Q: digital literacy has become
R: an essential skill
S: for every individual
questions.explanation: The subject 'digital literacy has become' (Q) is followed by the complement 'an essential skill' (R), then the modifier 'for every individual' (S), and finally 'in the modern world' (P). Thus, Q-R-S-P is the correct sequence.
questions.subject: English Language

questions.question: Match the prefixes/suffixes with their standard word formations in Column II:
questions.explanation: Mis- combines with understand (Misunderstand - II); -ful combines with hope (Hopeful - I); Un- combines with fortunate (Unfortunate - IV); -less combines with care (Careless - III).
questions.subject: English Language

questions.question: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word in the sentence: 'She sang very <u>sweetly</u> at the concert.'
questions.explanation: The word 'sweetly' modifies the verb 'sang', telling us *how* she sang. Words that modify verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs are adverbs.
questions.subject: English Language

questions.question: Directions: Given below are Assertion [As] and Reason [R]. Choose the correct option:
options: Both [As] and [R] are true, but [R] is not the correct explanation of [As].
Both [As] and [R] are true, and [R] is the correct explanation of [As].
questions.explanation: Assertion is false because 'university' begins with a consonant sound (/juːnɪˈvɜːsɪti/), so it takes 'a', not 'an'. Reason is true conceptually (articles depend on sound, not spelling). Thus, [As] is false, but [R] is true.
questions.assertion: The article 'an' is used before the word 'university'.
questions.reason: The choice of article ('a' or 'an') depends upon the initial vowel sound of the word, not just its spelling.
questions.subject: English Language

questions.question: Choose the correct synonym for the word 'ABUNDANT'.
questions.explanation: 'Abundant' means existing or available in large quantities; 'plentiful' is its direct synonym. Scarcely, meager, and deficient are antonyms or related to scarcity.
questions.subject: English Language
